Artificial intelligence (AI) adoption in UK financial services has continued to evolve since the Bank of England and FCA’s 2024 survey. Firms are using AI across a wider range of business areas and are increasingly reporting use of generative AI, AI-enabled agents and third-party implementations of AI systems. These developments may bring benefits for firms and consumers, including greater efficiency, improved decision support and stronger risk management. They may also create or amplify risks related to governance, operational resilience, data protection, consumer outcomes, third-party dependency and financial stability.

Given the pace of change, it is important that the Bank and FCA maintain an up-to-date understanding of how AI is being developed, deployed and overseen by UK financial services firms. This includes understanding how firms are adopting newer AI capabilities, how material those uses are, what benefits and risks firms perceive, and what controls, governance arrangements and constraints shape their use of AI.

The 2026 AI survey is part of the Bank and FCA’s wider programme of work on AI in UK financial services. This includes the previous AI/ML surveys in 2019, 2022 and 2024, the AI Public-Private Forum, Discussion Paper 5/22 and Feedback Statement 2/23 on Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, and the AI Consortium. It also includes related work by the Bank and FCA on operational resilience, critical third parties, model risk management, consumer outcomes and financial stability. The survey updates the authorities’ evidence base on how firms are using, governing and managing AI, and supports ongoing work as AI capabilities and adoption continue to evolve. Several findings – notably about uncertainty about best practice, third-party dependencies and readiness for more autonomous AI – also align with the Financial Services AI Adoption Plan published by the government’s independent AI Champions for financial services in July 2026.

This publication provides a descriptive summary of the aggregate survey results. It reports how respondent firms are using, planning to use, governing and managing AI, and how they perceive the associated benefits, risks and constraints. The findings should be read as evidence from participating firms, rather than as a complete assessment of AI adoption across the whole UK financial sector.

In previous surveys, all respondents completed the same full questionnaire. In 2026, to encourage participation from smaller firms, firms with fewer than 100 employees were given the option to complete a shorter questionnaire requiring less detailed information on their AI systems, although they could still choose to complete the full survey. Of the 196 respondents, there were 101 larger firms and 95 smaller firms. In total, 105 respondents completed the full survey. Unless otherwise stated, the figures presented in this report are based on responses to the full survey, to aid comparability with previous surveys. Section 10 summarises the responses to the short-form survey.

Unless otherwise stated, percentages in this report are calculated using valid question-level responses only (that is, excluding firms that did not answer the relevant question).

The results presented in this report are anonymised and aggregated with respondents grouped into the sectors listed in Table A.

UK deposit-takers, retail banks, building societies.

The survey received 196 responses with the number of respondents from each sector shown in Chart 1.

The 2026 survey retained core questions from previous surveys for continuity, while adding or amending questions to reflect developments in AI adoption and capability since 2024. Comparisons with 2024 should therefore be interpreted with care where question wording, definitions, scope or respondent populations differ.

Both the full and short-form survey asked respondents about their current use of AI.

AI adoption has continued to increase across respondent firms. Overall, across firms responding to the full and short-form surveys in 2026, 86% reported that they currently use AI. This continues the upward trends reported in previous surveys (75% in 2024 and 58% in 2022). Differences in respondent composition and question scope mean that the 2026 and 2024 percentages do not relate to the same population of firms and should therefore be compared with caution.

AI adoption was highest amongst banks and insurers. All responding UK banks and international banks reported currently using AI, followed by 93% of responding insurers (Chart 2).

The number of reported AI systems was uneven across firms. Almost half of firms responding to either the full or short-form survey reported ten or fewer AI systems (Chart 3). Around 10% of firms reported over 100 AI systems. Across all full and short-form survey responses, the ten firms reporting the highest number of AI systems accounted for 43% of all reported systems.

Distribution of respondents by number of reported AI systems

The full survey also asked respondents about the lifecycle stages of their AI systems, and their plans for future deployment.

AI deployment was near-universal among respondents to the full survey. The full survey also asked firms about the number of AI systems at different stages of the AI lifecycle. 94% reported having at least one AI system in production, rising cumulatively to 97% when systems in pilot or proof-of-concept were included, and to 99% when planned deployments over the next 12 months were also included.

Amongst respondents to the full survey, the median number of AI systems in production varied across sectors, with international banks and broker-dealers reporting the highest median (43 systems), followed by UK banks (22 systems), and insurance (18 systems).

Both the short-form and full survey asked firms to report their AI systems by business area.

Reported AI use was spread across business areas but remained concentrated in Operations and IT. This area accounted for approximately 31% of all reported AI systems, up from around 22% in 2024. No other individual area accounted for more than 11% of total AI systems. (Chart 4).

Share of all reported AI systems by business area and GenAI status

The survey included questions on firms' use of generative AI (GenAI), including foundation models and large language models (LLMs), across different business areas and sectors.

The reported technology mix has shifted substantially towards GenAI. In 2024, foundation models, including large language models, accounted for 17% of reported AI use cases. In 2026, GenAI systems accounted for 56% of all reported AI systems. While these measures capture different aspects of AI adoption and are therefore not directly comparable, taken together, they suggest a substantial increase in firms' reported use of general-purpose capabilities since 2024. The proportion of GenAI systems was material across all respondent sectors.
